units.rightText: There is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God, The holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High.

units.leftText: God is within her; she will not be moved. God will help her when morning dawns.
units.rightText: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God will help her, and that right early.

units.leftText: Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice.
units.rightText: The nations raged, the kingdoms were moved: He uttered his voice, the earth melted.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our refuge. [Selah*

units.leftText: Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation upon the earth.
units.rightText: Come, behold the works of Jehovah, What desolations he hath made in the earth.

units.leftText: He makes wars to cease throughout the earth; He breaks the bow and shatters the spear; He burns the shields in the fire.
units.rightText: He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; He breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; He burneth the chariots in the fire.
leftNotes: 46:9 Or chariots

units.leftText: “Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”
units.rightText: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our refuge. [Selah*

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph.
units.rightText: Oh clap your hands, all ye peoples; Shout unto God with the voice of triumph.

units.leftText: How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!
units.rightText: For Jehovah Most High is terrible; He is a great King over all the earth.

units.leftText: He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet.
units.rightText: He subdueth peoples under us, And nations under our feet.

units.leftText: He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah
units.rightText: He chooseth our inheritance for us, The glory of Jacob whom he loved. [Selah*

units.leftText: God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn.
units.rightText: God is gone up with a shout, Jehovah with the sound of a trumpet.

units.leftText: Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!
units.rightText: Sing praises to God, sing praises: Sing praises unto our King, sing praises.

units.leftText: For God is King of all the earth; sing to Him a psalm of praise.
units.rightText: For God is the King of all the earth: Sing ye praises with understanding.
leftNotes: 47:7 Or sing a Maskil of praise or sing praises with understanding

units.leftText: God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne.
units.rightText: God reigneth over the nations: God sitteth upon his holy throne.

units.leftText: The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.
units.rightText: The princes of the peoples are gathered together To be the people of the God of Abraham; For the shields of the earth belong unto God: He is greatly exalted.

units.leftText: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain.
units.rightText: Great is Jehovah, and greatly to be praised, In the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

units.leftText: Beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon is Mount Zion, the city of the great King.
units.rightText: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, Is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, The city of the great King.
leftNotes: 48:2 Or in the far north; the most sacred mountain of the Canaanites was Zaphon

units.leftText: God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress.
units.rightText: God hath made himself known in her palaces for a refuge.

units.leftText: For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together.
units.rightText: For, lo, the kings assembled themselves, They passed by together.

units.leftText: They saw and were astounded; they fled in terror.
units.rightText: They saw it, then were they amazed; They were dismayed, they hasted away.

units.leftText: Trembling seized them there, anguish like a woman in labor.
units.rightText: Trembling took hold of them there, Pain, as of a woman in travail.

units.leftText: With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish.
units.rightText: With the east wind Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish.
leftNotes: 48:7 Or a fleet of trading ships

units.leftText: As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah
units.rightText: As we have heard, so have we seen In the city of Jehovah of hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish it for ever. [Selah*

units.leftText: Within Your temple, O God, we contemplate Your loving devotion.
units.rightText: We have thought on thy lovingkindness, O God, In the midst of thy temple.

units.leftText: Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.
units.rightText: As is thy name, O God, So is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: Thy right hand is full of righteousness.

units.leftText: Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments.
units.rightText: Let mount Zion be glad, Let the daughters of Judah rejoice, Because of thy judgments.
leftNotes: 48:11 Or the villages

units.leftText: March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers,
units.rightText: Walk about Zion, and go round about her; Number the towers thereof;

units.leftText: consider her ramparts, tour her citadels, that you may tell the next generation.
units.rightText: Mark ye well her bulwarks; Consider her palaces: That ye may tell it to the generation following.

units.leftText: For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death.
units.rightText: For this God is our God for ever and ever: He will be our guide even unto death.
leftNotes: 48:14 Or He will guide us beyond death

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all inhabitants of the world,
units.rightText: Hear this, all ye peoples; Give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world,

units.leftText: both low and high, rich and poor alike.
units.rightText: Both low and high, Rich and poor together.

units.leftText: My mouth will impart wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding.
units.rightText: My mouth shall speak wisdom; And the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.

units.leftText: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will express my riddle with the harp:
units.rightText: I will incline mine ear to a parable: I will open my dark saying upon the harp.

units.leftText: Why should I fear in times of trouble, when wicked usurpers surround me?
units.rightText: Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, When iniquity at my heels compasseth me about?

units.leftText: They trust in their wealth and boast in their great riches.
units.rightText: They that trust in their wealth, And boast themselves in the multitude of their riches;

units.leftText: No man can possibly redeem his brother or pay his ransom to God.
units.rightText: None of them can by any means redeem his brother, Nor give to God a ransom for him
leftNotes: 49:7 Or redeem another

units.leftText: For the redemption of his soul is costly, and never can payment suffice,
units.rightText: (For the redemption of their life is costly, And it faileth for ever),

units.leftText: that he should live on forever and not see decay.
units.rightText: That he should still live alway, That he should not see corruption.

units.leftText: For it is clear that wise men die, and the foolish and the senseless both perish and leave their wealth to others.
units.rightText: For he shall see it. Wise men die; The fool and the brutish alike perish, And leave their wealth to others.

units.leftText: Their graves are their eternal homes — their dwellings for endless generations — even though their lands were their namesakes.
units.rightText: Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, And their dwelling-places to all generations; They call their lands after their own names.
leftNotes: 49:11 LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum; Hebrew Their inward thoughts

units.leftText: But a man, despite his wealth, cannot endure; he is like the beasts that perish.
units.rightText: But man being in honor abideth not: He is like the beasts that perish.

units.leftText: This is the fate of the foolish and their followers who endorse their sayings. Selah
units.rightText: This their way is their folly: Yet after them men approve their sayings. [Selah*
leftNotes: 49:13 Or the way of the foolish

units.leftText: Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
units.rightText: They are appointed as a flock for Sheol; Death shall be their shepherd: And the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; And their beauty shall be for Sheol to consume, That there be no habitation for it.

units.leftText: But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah
units.rightText: But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol; For he will receive me. [Selah*

units.leftText: Do not be afraid when a man grows rich, when the splendor of his house increases.
units.rightText: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, When the glory of his house is increased:

units.leftText: For when he dies, he will carry nothing away; his abundance will not follow him down.
units.rightText: For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away; His glory shall not descend after him.

units.leftText: Though in his lifetime he blesses his soul — and men praise you when you prosper —
units.rightText: Though while he lived he blessed his soul (And men praise thee, when thou doest well to thyself),

units.leftText: he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day.
units.rightText: He shall go to the generation of his fathers; They shall never see the light.

units.leftText: A man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish.
units.rightText: Man that is in honor, and understandeth not, Is like the beasts that perish.

units.leftText: A Psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.
units.rightText: The Mighty One, God, Jehovah, hath spoken, And called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.

units.leftText: From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
units.rightText: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined forth.

units.leftText: Our God approaches and will not be silent! Consuming fire precedes Him, and a tempest rages around Him.
units.rightText: Our God cometh, and doth not keep silence: A fire devoureth before him, And it is very tempestuous round about him.

units.leftText: He summons the heavens above, and the earth, that He may judge His people:
units.rightText: He calleth to the heavens above, And to the earth, that he may judge his people:

units.leftText: “Gather to Me My saints, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.”
units.rightText: Gather my saints together unto me, Those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.

units.leftText: And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge. Selah
units.rightText: And the heavens shall declare his righteousness; For God is judge himself. [Selah*
leftNotes: 50:6 Or He is a God of justice

units.leftText: “Hear, O My people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God.
units.rightText: Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify unto thee: I am God, even thy God.

units.leftText: I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before Me.
units.rightText: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices; And thy burnt-offerings are continually before me.

units.leftText: I have no need for a bull from your stall or goats from your pens,
units.rightText: I will take no bullock out of thy house, Nor he-goats out of thy folds.

units.leftText: for every beast of the forest is Mine — the cattle on a thousand hills.
units.rightText: For every beast of the forest is mine, And the cattle upon a thousand hills.

units.leftText: I know every bird in the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.
units.rightText: I know all the birds of the mountains; And the wild beasts of the field are mine.

units.leftText: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and the fullness thereof.
units.rightText: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee; For the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.

units.leftText: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
units.rightText: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, Or drink the blood of goats?

units.leftText: Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
units.rightText: Offer unto God the sacrifice of thanksgiving; And pay thy vows unto the Most High;

units.leftText: Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.”
units.rightText: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

units.leftText: To the wicked, however, God says, “What right have you to recite My statutes and to bear My covenant on your lips?
units.rightText: But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, And that thou hast taken my covenant in thy mouth,

units.leftText: For you hate My instruction and cast My words behind you.
units.rightText: Seeing that thou hatest instruction, And castest my words behind thee?

units.leftText: When you see a thief, you befriend him, and throw in your lot with adulterers.
units.rightText: When thou sawest a thief, thou consentedst with him, And hast been partaker with adulterers.

units.leftText: You unleash your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit.
units.rightText: Thou givest thy mouth to evil, And thy tongue frameth deceit.

units.leftText: You sit and malign your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.
units.rightText: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.

units.leftText: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
units.rightText: These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such a one as thyself: But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.
leftNotes: 50:21 Or you thought the ‘I AM’ was
50:21 Literally and I set it in order before your eyes

units.leftText: Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you:
units.rightText: Now consider this, ye that forget God, Lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver:

units.leftText: He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God.”
units.rightText: Whoso offereth the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifieth me; And to him that ordereth his way aright Will I show the salvation of God.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
units.rightText: Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
leftNotes: 51:1 Or Be gracious to me

units.leftText: Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.
units.rightText: Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, And cleanse me from my sin.

units.leftText: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
units.rightText: For I know my transgressions; And my sin is ever before me.

units.leftText: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
units.rightText: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, And done that which is evil in thy sight; That thou mayest be justified when thou speakest, And be clear when thou judgest.
leftNotes: 51:4 LXX and victorious when You judge; cited in Romans 3:4|ROM 3:4*

units.leftText: Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
units.rightText: Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity; And in sin did my mother conceive me.

units.leftText: Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
units.rightText: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts; And in the hidden part thou wilt make me to know wisdom.

units.leftText: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
units.rightText: Purify me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

units.leftText: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.
units.rightText: Make me to hear joy and gladness, That the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.

units.leftText: Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities.
units.rightText: Hide thy face from my sins, And blot out all mine iniquities.

units.leftText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.
units.rightText: Create in me a clean heart, O God; And renew a right spirit within me.

units.leftText: Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me.
units.rightText: Cast me not away from thy presence; And take not thy holy Spirit from me.

units.leftText: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
units.rightText: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with a willing spirit.

units.leftText: Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.
units.rightText: Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee.

units.leftText: Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.
units.rightText: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation; And my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.

units.leftText: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.
units.rightText: O Lord, open thou my lips; And my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

units.leftText: For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.
units.rightText: For thou delightest not in sacrifice; else would I give it: Thou hast no pleasure in burnt-offering.

units.leftText: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
units.rightText: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: A broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

units.leftText: In Your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion: Build thou the walls of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar.
units.rightText: Then wilt thou delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, In burnt-offering and whole burnt-offering: Then will they offer bullocks upon thine altar.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.” Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long.
units.rightText: Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? The lovingkindness of God endureth continually.
leftNotes: 52:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.
units.rightText: Thy tongue deviseth very wickedness, Like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.

units.leftText: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah
units.rightText: Thou lovest evil more than good, And lying rather than to speak righteousness. [Selah*

units.leftText: You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue.
units.rightText: Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.

units.leftText: Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
units.rightText: God will likewise destroy thee for ever; He will take thee up, and pluck thee out of thy tent, And root thee out of the land of the living. [Selah*

units.leftText: The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying,
units.rightText: The righteous also shall see it, and fear, And shall laugh at him, saying,

units.leftText: “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”
units.rightText: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, But trusted in the abundance of his riches, And strengthened himself in his wickedness.

units.leftText: But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.
units.rightText: But as for me, I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God: I trust in the lovingkindness of God for ever and ever.

units.leftText: I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name — for it is good — in the presence of Your saints.
units.rightText: I will give thee thanks for ever, because thou hast done it; And I will hope in thy name, for it is good, in the presence of thy saints.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good.
units.rightText: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity; There is none that doeth good.
leftNotes: 53:1 Mahalathis probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 88:1|PSA 88:1*.
53:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
units.rightText: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, To see if there were any that did understand, That did seek after God.

units.leftText: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
units.rightText: Every one of them is gone back; they are together become filthy; There is none that doeth good, no, not one.
leftNotes: 53:3 LXX worthless
53:3 Cited in Romans 3:10–12|ROM 3:10-12*

units.leftText: Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God.
units.rightText: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, Who eat up my people as they eat bread, And call not upon God?

units.leftText: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.
units.rightText: There were they in great fear, where no fear was; For God hath scattered the bones of him that encampeth against thee: Thou hast put them to shame, because God hath rejected them.

units.leftText: Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
units.rightText: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion! When God bringeth back the captivity of his people, Then shall Jacob rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
leftNotes: 53:6 Or the fortunes of His people

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. When the Ziphites went to Saul and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might!
units.rightText: Save me, O God, by thy name, And judge me in thy might.
leftNotes: 54:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Hear my prayer, O God; Give ear to the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life — men with no regard for God. Selah
units.rightText: For strangers are risen up against me, And violent men have sought after my soul: They have not set God before them. [Selah*

units.leftText: Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.
units.rightText: Behold, God is my helper: The Lord is of them that uphold my soul.

units.leftText: He will reward my enemies with evil. In Your faithfulness, destroy them.
units.rightText: He will requite the evil unto mine enemies: Destroy thou them in thy truth.

units.leftText: Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good.
units.rightText: With a freewill-offering will I sacrifice unto thee: I will give thanks unto thy name, O Jehovah, for it is good.

units.leftText: For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eyes have looked in triumph on my foes.
units.rightText: For he hath delivered me out of all trouble; And mine eye hath seen my desire upon mine enemies.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea.
units.rightText: Give ear to my prayer, O God; And hide not thyself from my supplication.
leftNotes: 55:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint,
units.rightText: Attend unto me, and answer me: I am restless in my complaint, and moan,

units.leftText: at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster upon me and resent me in their anger.
units.rightText: Because of the voice of the enemy, Because of the oppression of the wicked; For they cast iniquity upon me, And in anger they persecute me.

units.leftText: My heart pounds within me, and the terrors of death assail me.
units.rightText: My heart is sore pained within me: And the terrors of death are fallen upon me.

units.leftText: Fear and trembling grip me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
units.rightText: Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, And horror hath overwhelmed me.

units.leftText: I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.
units.rightText: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then would I fly away, and be at rest.

units.leftText: How far away I would flee! In the wilderness I would remain. Selah
units.rightText: Lo, then would I wander far off, I would lodge in the wilderness. [Selah*

units.leftText: I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest.”
units.rightText: I would haste me to a shelter From the stormy wind and tempest.

units.leftText: O Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.
units.rightText: Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongue; For I have seen violence and strife in the city.

units.leftText: Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within.
units.rightText: Day and night they go about it upon the walls thereof: Iniquity also and mischief are in the midst of it.

units.leftText: Destruction is within; oppression and deceit never leave the streets.
units.rightText: Wickedness is in the midst thereof: Oppression and guile depart not from its streets.

units.leftText: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
units.rightText: For it was not an enemy that reproached me; Then I could have borne it: Neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; Then I would have hid myself from him:

units.leftText: But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.
units.rightText: But it was thou, a man mine equal, My companion, and my familiar friend.

units.leftText: We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
units.rightText: We took sweet counsel together; We walked in the house of God with the throng.

units.leftText: Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes.
units.rightText: Let death come suddenly upon them, Let them go down alive into Sheol; For wickedness is in their dwelling, in the midst of them.

units.leftText: But I call to God, and the LORD saves me.
units.rightText: As for me, I will call upon God; And Jehovah will save me.

units.leftText: Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice.
units.rightText: Evening, and morning, and at noonday, will I complain, and moan; And he will hear my voice.

units.leftText: He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me.
units.rightText: He hath redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me; For they were many that strove with me.

units.leftText: God will hear and humiliate them — the One enthroned for the ages — Selah because they do not change and they have no fear of God.
units.rightText: God will hear, and answer them, Even he that abideth of old, [Selah* The men who have no changes, And who fear not God.

units.leftText: My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant.
units.rightText: He hath put forth his hands against such as were at peace with him: He hath profaned his covenant.

units.leftText: His speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed.
units.rightText: His mouth was smooth as butter, But his heart was war: His words were softer than oil, Yet were they drawn swords.

units.leftText: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
units.rightText: Cast thy burden upon Jehovah, and he will sustain thee: He will never suffer the righteous to be moved.

units.leftText: But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.
units.rightText: But thou, O God, wilt bring them down into the pit of destruction: Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; But I will trust in thee.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.
units.rightText: Be merciful unto me, O God; for man would swallow me up: All the day long he fighting oppresseth me.
leftNotes: 56:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me.
units.rightText: Mine enemies would swallow me up all the day long; For they are many that fight proudly against me.

units.leftText: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
units.rightText: What time I am afraid, I will put my trust in thee.

units.leftText: In God, whose word I praise — in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
units.rightText: In God (I will praise his word), In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can flesh do unto me?

units.leftText: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise.
units.rightText: All the day long they wrest my words: All their thoughts are against me for evil.

units.leftText: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.
units.rightText: They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, They mark my steps, Even as they have waited for my soul.

units.leftText: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
units.rightText: Shall they escape by iniquity? In anger cast down the peoples, O God.
leftNotes: 56:7 Or do not let them escape; MT does not include do not.

units.leftText: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle — are they not in Your book?
units.rightText: Thou numberest my wanderings: Put thou my tears into thy bottle; Are they not in thy book?
leftNotes: 56:8 Or sorrows

units.leftText: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.
units.rightText: Then shall mine enemies turn back in the day that I call: This I know, that God is for me.

units.leftText: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
units.rightText: In God (I will praise his word), In Jehovah (I will praise his word),

units.leftText: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
units.rightText: In God have I put my trust, I will not be afraid; What can man do unto me?

units.leftText: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.
units.rightText: Thy vows are upon me, O God: I will render thank-offerings unto thee.

units.leftText: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.
units.rightText: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: Hast thou not delivered my feet from falling, That I may walk before God In the light of the living?

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed.
units.rightText: Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me; For my soul taketh refuge in thee: Yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I take refuge, Until these calamities be overpast.
leftNotes: 57:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.
units.rightText: I will cry unto God Most High, Unto God that performeth all things for me.
leftNotes: 57:2 Hebrew Elohim-Elyon

units.leftText: He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth.
units.rightText: He will send from heaven, and save me, When he that would swallow me up reproacheth; [Selah* God will send forth his lovingkindness and his truth.

units.leftText: My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts— with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
units.rightText: My soul is among lions; I lie among them that are set on fire, Even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, And their tongue a sharp sword.

units.leftText: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
units.rightText: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; Let thy glory be above all the earth.

units.leftText: They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah
units.rightText: They have prepared a net for my steps; My soul is bowed down: They have digged a pit before me; They are fallen into the midst thereof themselves. [Selah*

units.leftText: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music.
units.rightText: My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing, yea, I will sing praises.

units.leftText: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
units.rightText: Awake up, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake right early.
leftNotes: 57:8 Or Awake, my soul!

units.leftText: I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples.
units.rightText: I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the peoples: I will sing praises unto thee among the nations.

units.leftText: For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds.
units.rightText: For thy lovingkindness is great unto the heavens, And thy truth unto the skies.

units.leftText: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
units.rightText: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; Let thy glory be above all the earth.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David. Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
units.rightText: Do ye indeed in silence speak righteousness? Do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
leftNotes: 58:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.
units.rightText: Nay, in heart ye work wickedness; Ye weigh out the violence of your hands in the earth.

units.leftText: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.
units.rightText: The wicked are estranged from the womb: They go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies.

units.leftText: Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,
units.rightText: Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: They are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear,

units.leftText: refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.
units.rightText: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of charmers, Charming never so wisely.

units.leftText: O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
units.rightText: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: Break out the great teeth of the young lions, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
units.rightText: Let them melt away as water that runneth apace: When he aimeth his arrows, let them be as though they were cut off.
leftNotes: 58:7 Or when they are trodden down, may they wither like grass

units.leftText: Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
units.rightText: Let them be as a snail which melteth and passeth away, Like the untimely birth of a woman, that hath not seen the sun.

units.leftText: Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.
units.rightText: Before your pots can feel the thorns, He will take them away with a whirlwind, the green and the burning alike.

units.leftText: The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
units.rightText: The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked;

units.leftText: Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”
units.rightText: So that men shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: Verily there is a God that judgeth in the earth.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise against me.
units.rightText: Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: Set me on high from them that rise up against me.
leftNotes: 59:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed.
units.rightText: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity, And save me from the bloodthirsty men.

units.leftText: See how they lie in wait for me. Fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of my own, O LORD.
units.rightText: For, lo, they lie in wait for my soul; The mighty gather themselves together against me: Not for my transgression, nor for my sin, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: For no fault of my own, they move swiftly to attack me. Arise to help me, and take notice.
units.rightText: They run and prepare themselves without my fault: Awake thou to help me, and behold.

units.leftText: O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah
units.rightText: Even thou, O Jehovah God of hosts, the God of Israel, Arise to visit all the nations: Be not merciful to any wicked transgressors. [Selah*

units.leftText: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
units.rightText: They return at evening, they howl like a dog, And go round about the city.

units.leftText: See what they spew from their mouths— sharp words from their lips: “For who can hear us?”
units.rightText: Behold, they belch out with their mouth; Swords are in their lips: For who, say they, doth hear?

units.leftText: But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.
units.rightText: But thou, O Jehovah, wilt laugh at them; Thou wilt have all the nations in derision.

units.leftText: I will keep watch for You, O my strength, because You, O God, are my fortress.
units.rightText: Because of his strength I will give heed unto thee; For God is my high tower.

units.leftText: My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes.
units.rightText: My God with his lovingkindness will meet me: God will let me see my desire upon mine enemies.

units.leftText: Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
units.rightText: Slay them not, lest my people forget: Scatter them by thy power, and bring them down, O Lord our shield.

units.leftText: By the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter.
units.rightText: For the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, Let them even be taken in their pride, And for cursing and lying which they speak.

units.leftText: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, so it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah
units.rightText: Consume them in wrath, consume them, so that they shall be no more: And let them know that God ruleth in Jacob, Unto the ends of the earth. [Selah*

units.leftText: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
units.rightText: And at evening let them return, let them howl like a dog, And go round about the city.

units.leftText: They scavenge for food, and growl if they are not satisfied.
units.rightText: They shall wander up and down for food, And tarry all night if they be not satisfied.

units.leftText: But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.
units.rightText: But I will sing of thy strength; Yea, I will sing aloud of thy lovingkindness in the morning: For thou hast been my high tower, And a refuge in the day of my distress.

units.leftText: To You, O my strength, I sing praises, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion.
units.rightText: Unto thee, O my strength, will I sing praises: For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
units.rightText: O God thou hast cast us off, thou hast broken us down; Thou hast been angry; oh restore us again.
leftNotes: 60:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.
60:1 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.
60:1 That is, the land northeast of Damascus

units.leftText: You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.
units.rightText: Thou hast made the land to tremble; thou hast rent it: Heal the breaches thereof; for it shaketh.

units.leftText: You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.
units.rightText: Thou hast showed thy people hard things: Thou hast made us to drink the wine of staggering.

units.leftText: You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah
units.rightText: Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, That it may be displayed because of the truth. [Selah*
leftNotes: 60:4 Or that it may be displayed because of truth

units.leftText: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
units.rightText: That thy beloved may be delivered, Save with thy right hand, and answer us.

units.leftText: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
units.rightText: God hath spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth.
leftNotes: 60:6 Or in His holiness

units.leftText: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
units.rightText: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the defence of my head; Judah is my sceptre.

units.leftText: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
units.rightText: Moab is my washpot; Upon Edom will I cast my shoe: Philistia, shout thou because of me.

units.leftText: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
units.rightText: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who hath led me unto Edom?

units.leftText: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
units.rightText: Hast not thou, O God, cast us off? And thou goest not forth, O God, with our hosts.

units.leftText: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
units.rightText: Give us help against the adversary; For vain is the help of man.

units.leftText: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.
units.rightText: Through God we shall do valiantly; For he it is that will tread down our adversaries.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
units.rightText: Hear my cry, O God; Attend unto my prayer.

units.leftText: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
units.rightText: From the end of the earth will I call unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

units.leftText: For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.
units.rightText: For thou hast been a refuge for me, A strong tower from the enemy.

units.leftText: Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
units.rightText: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever: I will take refuge in the covert of thy wings. [Selah*

units.leftText: For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name.
units.rightText: For thou, O God, hast heard my vows: Thou hast given me the heritage of those that fear thy name.

units.leftText: Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations.
units.rightText: Thou wilt prolong the king’s life; His years shall be as many generations.

units.leftText: May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him.
units.rightText: He shall abide before God for ever: Oh prepare lovingkindness and truth, that they may preserve him.

units.leftText: Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day.
units.rightText: So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, That I may daily perform my vows.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.
units.rightText: My soul waiteth in silence for God only: From him cometh my salvation.

units.leftText: He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken.
units.rightText: He only is my rock and my salvation: He is my high tower; I shall not be greatly moved.

units.leftText: How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence?
units.rightText: How long will ye set upon a man, That ye may slay him, all of you, Like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?

units.leftText: They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah
units.rightText: They only consult to thrust him down from his dignity; They delight in lies; They bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. [Selah*

units.leftText: Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
units.rightText: My soul, wait thou in silence for God only; For my expectation is from him.

units.leftText: He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.
units.rightText: He only is my rock and my salvation: He is my high tower; I shall not be moved.

units.leftText: My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God.
units.rightText: With God is my salvation and my glory: The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.

units.leftText: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah
units.rightText: Trust in him at all times, ye people; Pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. [Selah*

units.leftText: Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor.
units.rightText: Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: In the balances they will go up; They are together lighter than vanity.

units.leftText: Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
units.rightText: Trust not in oppression, And become not vain in robbery: If riches increase, set not your heart thereon.

units.leftText: God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God,
units.rightText: God hath spoken once, Twice have I heard this, That power belongeth unto God.

units.leftText: and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.
units.rightText: Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth lovingkindness; For thou renderest to every man according to his work.
leftNotes: 62:12 Cited in Romans 2:6|ROM 2:6*

units.leftText: A Psalm of David, when he was in the Wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water.
units.rightText: O God, thou art my God; earnestly will I seek thee: My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee, In a dry and weary land, where no water is.

units.leftText: So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory.
units.rightText: So have I looked upon thee in the sanctuary, To see thy power and thy glory.

units.leftText: Because Your loving devotion is better than life, my lips will glorify You.
units.rightText: Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, My lips shall praise thee.

units.leftText: So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands.
units.rightText: So will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name.

units.leftText: My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods; with joyful lips my mouth will praise You.
units.rightText: My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; And my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips;

units.leftText: When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night.
units.rightText: When I remember thee upon my bed, And meditate on thee in the night-watches.

units.leftText: For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.
units.rightText: For thou hast been my help, And in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.

units.leftText: My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.
units.rightText: My soul followeth hard after thee: Thy right hand upholdeth me.

units.leftText: But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth.
units.rightText: But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, Shall go into the lower parts of the earth.

units.leftText: They will fall to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for foxes.
units.rightText: They shall be given over to the power of the sword: They shall be a portion for foxes.

units.leftText: But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be shut.
units.rightText: But the king shall rejoice in God: Every one that sweareth by him shall glory; For the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy.
units.rightText: Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint: Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

units.leftText: Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity,
units.rightText: Hide me from the secret counsel of evil-doers, From the tumult of the workers of iniquity;

units.leftText: who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows,
units.rightText: Who have whet their tongue like a sword, And have aimed their arrows, even bitter words,

units.leftText: ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear.
units.rightText: That they may shoot in secret places at the perfect: Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.

units.leftText: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they speak of hiding their snares. “Who will see them?” they say.
units.rightText: They encourage themselves in an evil purpose; They commune of laying snares privily; They say, Who will see them?

units.leftText: They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious.
units.rightText: They search out iniquities; We have accomplished, say they, a diligent search: And the inward thought and the heart of every one is deep.

units.leftText: But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.
units.rightText: But God will shoot at them; With an arrow suddenly shall they be wounded.

units.leftText: They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads.
units.rightText: So they shall be made to stumble, their own tongue being against them: All that see them shall wag the head.

units.leftText: Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God; so they will ponder what He has done.
units.rightText: And all men shall fear; And they shall declare the work of God, And shall wisely consider of his doing.

units.leftText: Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult.
units.rightText: The righteous shall be glad in Jehovah, and shall take refuge in him; And all the upright in heart shall glory.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion; to You our vows will be fulfilled.
units.rightText: Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Zion; And unto thee shall the vow be performed.

units.leftText: O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You.
units.rightText: O thou that hearest prayer, Unto thee shall all flesh come.

units.leftText: When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions.
units.rightText: Iniquities prevail against me: As for our transgressions, thou wilt forgive them.

units.leftText: Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts! We are filled with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest, and causest to approach unto thee, That he may dwell in thy courts: We shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, Thy holy temple.

units.leftText: With awesome deeds of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
units.rightText: By terrible things thou wilt answer us in righteousness, O God of our salvation, Thou that art the confidence of all the ends of the earth, And of them that are afar off upon the sea:

units.leftText: You formed the mountains by Your power, having girded Yourself with might.
units.rightText: Who by his strength setteth fast the mountains, Being girded about with might;

units.leftText: You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves, and the tumult of the nations.
units.rightText: Who stilleth the roaring of the seas, The roaring of their waves, And the tumult of the peoples.

units.leftText: Those who live far away fear Your wonders; You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy.
units.rightText: They also that dwell in the uttermost parts are afraid at thy tokens: Thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice.
leftNotes: 65:8 Or where morning dawns and evening fades You call forth songs of joy.

units.leftText: You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it. The streams of God are full of water, for You prepare our grain by providing for the earth.
units.rightText: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it, Thou greatly enrichest it; The river of God is full of water: Thou providest them grain, when thou hast so prepared the earth.
leftNotes: 65:9 Or and make it overflow
65:9 Or to provide the people with grain, for so You have ordained it

units.leftText: You soak its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth.
units.rightText: Thou waterest its furrows abundantly; Thou settlest the ridges thereof: Thou makest it soft with showers; Thou blessest the springing thereof.

units.leftText: You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty.
units.rightText: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; And thy paths drop fatness.

units.leftText: The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy.
units.rightText: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness; And the hills are girded with joy.

units.leftText: The pastures are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain. They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.
units.rightText: The pastures are clothed with flocks; The valleys also are covered over with grain; They shout for joy, they also sing.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A song. A Psalm. Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!
units.rightText: Make a joyful noise unto God, all the earth:

units.leftText: Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
units.rightText: Sing forth the glory of his name: Make his praise glorious.

units.leftText: Say to God, “How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You.
units.rightText: Say unto God, How terrible are thy works! Through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.

units.leftText: All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name.” Selah
units.rightText: All the earth shall worship thee, And shall sing unto thee; They shall sing to thy name. [Selah*

units.leftText: Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind.
units.rightText: Come, and see the works of God; He is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.

units.leftText: He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.
units.rightText: He turned the sea into dry land; They went through the river on foot: There did we rejoice in him.

units.leftText: He rules forever by His power; His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah
units.rightText: He ruleth by his might for ever; His eyes observe the nations: Let not the rebellious exalt themselves. [Selah*

units.leftText: Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard.
units.rightText: Oh bless our God, ye peoples, And make the voice of his praise to be heard;

units.leftText: He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping.
units.rightText: Who holdeth our soul in life, And suffereth not our feet to be moved.

units.leftText: For You , O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver.
units.rightText: For thou, O God, hast proved us: Thou hast tried us, as silver is tried.

units.leftText: You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs.
units.rightText: Thou broughtest us into the net; Thou layedst a sore burden upon our loins.

units.leftText: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance.
units.rightText: Thou didst cause men to ride over our heads; We went through fire and through water; But thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.

units.leftText: I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You —
units.rightText: I will come into thy house with burnt-offerings; I will pay thee my vows,

units.leftText: the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress.
units.rightText: Which my lips uttered, And my mouth spake, when I was in distress.

units.leftText: I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah
units.rightText: I will offer unto thee burnt-offerings of fatlings, With the incense of rams; I will offer bullocks with goats. [Selah*

units.leftText: Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me.
units.rightText: Come, and hear, all ye that fear God, And I will declare what he hath done for my soul.

units.leftText: I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue.
units.rightText: I cried unto him with my mouth, And he was extolled with my tongue.
leftNotes: 66:17 Or and His praise was on my tongue

units.leftText: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
units.rightText: If I regard iniquity in my heart, The Lord will not hear:

units.leftText: But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer.
units.rightText: But verily God hath heard; He hath attended to the voice of my prayer.

units.leftText: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!
units.rightText: Blessed be God, Who hath not turned away my prayer, Nor his lovingkindness from me.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song. May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah
units.rightText: God be merciful unto us, and bless us, And cause his face to shine upon us; [Selah*

units.leftText: that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
units.rightText: That thy way may be known upon earth, Thy salvation among all nations.

units.leftText: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
units.rightText: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.

units.leftText: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah
units.rightText: Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy; For thou wilt judge the peoples with equity, And govern the nations upon earth. [Selah*

units.leftText: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
units.rightText: Let the peoples praise thee, O God; Let all the peoples praise thee.

units.leftText: The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
units.rightText: The earth hath yielded its increase: God, even our own God, will bless us.

units.leftText: God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him.
units.rightText: God will bless us; And all the ends of the earth shall fear him.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. God arises. His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence.
units.rightText: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; Let them also that hate him flee before him.

units.leftText: As smoke is blown away, You will drive them out; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish in the presence of God.
units.rightText: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: As wax melteth before the fire, So let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

units.leftText: But the righteous will be glad and rejoice before God; they will celebrate with joy.
units.rightText: But let the righteous be glad; let them exult before God: Yea, let them rejoice with gladness.

units.leftText: Sing to God! Sing praises to His name. Exalt Him who rides on the clouds — His name is the LORD— and rejoice before Him.
units.rightText: Sing unto God, sing praises to his name: Cast up a highway for him that rideth through the deserts; His name is Jehovah; and exult ye before him.
leftNotes: 68:4 Or rides through the deserts

units.leftText: A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation.
units.rightText: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, Is God in his holy habitation.

units.leftText: God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
units.rightText: God setteth the solitary in families: He bringeth out the prisoners into prosperity; But the rebellious dwell in a parched land.

units.leftText: O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wasteland, Selah
units.rightText: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, When thou didst march through the wilderness; [Selah*

units.leftText: the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: The earth trembled, The heavens also dropped rain at the presence of God: Yon Sinai trembled at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: You sent abundant rain, O God; You refreshed Your weary inheritance.
units.rightText: Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain, Thou didst confirm thine inheritance, when it was weary.

units.leftText: Your flock settled therein; O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor.
units.rightText: Thy congregation dwelt therein: Thou, O God, didst prepare of thy goodness for the poor.

units.leftText: The Lord gives the command; a great company of women proclaim it:
units.rightText: The Lord giveth the word: The women that publish the tidings are a great host.

units.leftText: “Kings and their armies flee in haste; she who waits at home divides the plunder.
units.rightText: Kings of armies flee, they flee; And she that tarrieth at home divideth the spoil.

units.leftText: Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold.”
units.rightText: When ye lie among the sheepfolds, It is as the wings of a dove covered with silver, And her pinions with yellow gold.

units.leftText: When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon.
units.rightText: When the Almighty scattered kings therein, It was as when it snoweth in Zalmon.
leftNotes: 68:14 Hebrew Shaddai

units.leftText: A mountain of God is Mount Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan.
units.rightText: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; A high mountain is the mountain of Bashan.

units.leftText: Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever.
units.rightText: Why look ye askance, ye high mountains, At the mountain which God hath desired for his abode? Yea, Jehovah will dwell in it for ever.

units.leftText: The chariots of God are tens of thousands — thousands of thousands are they; the Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai.
units.rightText: The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands upon thousands: The Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in the sanctuary.
leftNotes: 68:17 Or the Lord has come from Sinai in His holiness

units.leftText: You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts from men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.
units.rightText: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led away captives; Thou hast received gifts among men, Yea, among the rebellious also, that Jehovah God might dwell with them.
leftNotes: 68:18 Cited in Ephesians 4:8|EPH 4:8*

units.leftText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah
units.rightText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily beareth our burden, Even the God who is our salvation. [Selah*

units.leftText: Our God is a God of deliverance; the Lord GOD is our rescuer from death.
units.rightText: God is unto us a God of deliverances; And unto Jehovah the Lord belongeth escape from death.

units.leftText: Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways.
units.rightText: But God will smite through the head of his enemies, The hairy scalp of such a one as goeth on still in his guiltiness.

units.leftText: The Lord said, “I will retrieve them from Bashan, I will bring them up from the depths of the sea,
units.rightText: The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring them again from the depths of the sea;

units.leftText: that your foot may be dipped in the blood of your foes— the tongues of your dogs in the same.”
units.rightText: That thou mayest crush them, dipping thy foot in blood, That the tongue of thy dogs may have its portion from thine enemies.

units.leftText: They have seen Your procession, O God — the march of my God and King into the sanctuary.
units.rightText: They have seen thy goings, O God, Even the goings of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.

units.leftText: The singers lead the way, the musicians follow after, among the maidens playing tambourines.
units.rightText: The singers went before, the minstrels followed after, In the midst of the damsels playing with timbrels.

units.leftText: Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.
units.rightText: Bless ye God in the congregations, Even the Lord, ye that are of the fountain of Israel.

units.leftText: There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah in their company, the princes of Zebulun and of Naphtali.
units.rightText: There is little Benjamin their ruler, The princes of Judah and their council, The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.

units.leftText: Summon Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have exerted on our behalf.
units.rightText: Thy God hath commanded thy strength: Strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.
leftNotes: 68:28 LXX and Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts Your God has summoned your power

units.leftText: Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings will bring You gifts.
units.rightText: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem Kings shall bring presents unto thee.

units.leftText: Rebuke the beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war.
units.rightText: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, The multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples, Trampling under foot the pieces of silver: He hath scattered the peoples that delight in war.

units.leftText: Envoys will arrive from Egypt; Cush will stretch out her hands to God.
units.rightText: Princes shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall haste to stretch out her hands unto God.
leftNotes: 68:31 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord— Selah
units.rightText: Sing unto God, ye kingdoms of the earth; Oh sing praises unto the Lord; [Selah*

units.leftText: to Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old; behold, His mighty voice resounds.
units.rightText: To him that rideth upon the heaven of heavens, which are of old; Lo, he uttereth his voice, a mighty voice.

units.leftText: Ascribe the power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose strength is in the skies.
units.rightText: Ascribe ye strength unto God: His excellency is over Israel, And his strength is in the skies.

units.leftText: O God, You are awesome in Your sanctuary; the God of Israel Himself gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God!
units.rightText: O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: The God of Israel, he giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.
units.rightText: Save me, O God; For the waters are come in unto my soul.

units.leftText: I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me.
units.rightText: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

units.leftText: I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
units.rightText: I am weary with my crying; my throat is dried: Mine eyes fail while I wait for my God.

units.leftText: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me — my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay.
units.rightText: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: They that would cut me off, being mine enemies wrongfully, are mighty: That which I took not away I have to restore.

units.leftText: You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
units.rightText: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; And my sins are not hid from thee.

units.leftText: May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored through me, O God of Israel.
units.rightText: Let not them that wait for thee be put to shame through me, O Lord Jehovah of hosts: Let not those that seek thee be brought to dishonor through me, O God of Israel.

units.leftText: For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.
units.rightText: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; Shame hath covered my face.

units.leftText: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,
units.rightText: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, And an alien unto my mother’s children.

units.leftText: because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
units.rightText: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; And the reproaches of them that reproach thee are fallen upon me.
leftNotes: 69:9 Cited in John 2:17|JHN 2:17*
69:9 Cited in Romans 15:3|ROM 15:3*

units.leftText: I wept and fasted, but it brought me reproach.
units.rightText: When I wept, and chastened my soul with fasting, That was to my reproach.

units.leftText: I made sackcloth my clothing, and I was sport to them.
units.rightText: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword unto them.

units.leftText: Those who sit at the gate mock me, and I am the song of drunkards.
units.rightText: They that sit in the gate talk of me; And I am the song of the drunkards.

units.leftText: But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor. In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation.
units.rightText: But as for me, my prayer is unto thee, O Jehovah, in an acceptable time: O God, in the abundance of thy lovingkindness, Answer me in the truth of thy salvation.

units.leftText: Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters.
units.rightText: Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink: Let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

units.leftText: Do not let the floods engulf me or the depths swallow me up; let not the Pit close its mouth over me.
units.rightText: Let not the waterflood overwhelm me, Neither let the deep swallow me up; And let not the pit shut its mouth upon me.

units.leftText: Answer me, O LORD, for Your loving devotion is good; turn to me in keeping with Your great compassion.
units.rightText: Answer me, O Jehovah; for thy lovingkindness is good: According to the multitude of thy tender mercies turn thou unto me.

units.leftText: Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!
units.rightText: And hide not thy face from thy servant; For I am in distress; answer me speedily.

units.leftText: Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes.
units.rightText: Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it: Ransom me because of mine enemies.

units.leftText: You know my reproach, my shame and disgrace. All my adversaries are before You.
units.rightText: Thou knowest my reproach, and my shame, and my dishonor: Mine adversaries are all before thee.

units.leftText: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one.
units.rightText: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: And I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; And for comforters, but I found none.

units.leftText: They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.
units.rightText: They gave me also gall for my food; And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

units.leftText: May their table become a snare; may it be a retribution and a trap.
units.rightText: Let their table before them become a snare; And when they are in peace, let it become a trap.
leftNotes: 69:22 A slight revocalization of the Hebrew (see also LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate); literally may their prosperity be a trap; cited in Romans 11:9|ROM 11:9*

units.leftText: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.
units.rightText: Let their eyes be darkened, so that they cannot see; And make their loins continually to shake.
leftNotes: 69:23 LXX; Hebrew and may their loins tremble continually; cited in Romans 11:10|ROM 11:10*

units.leftText: Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
units.rightText: Pour out thine indignation upon them, And let the fierceness of thine anger overtake them.
