units.leftText: May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents.
units.rightText: Let their habitation be desolate; Let none dwell in their tents.
leftNotes: 69:25 Cited in Acts 1:20|ACT 1:20*

units.leftText: For they persecute the one You struck and recount the pain of those You wounded.
units.rightText: For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; And they tell of the sorrow of those whom thou hast wounded.

units.leftText: Add iniquity to their iniquity; let them not share in Your righteousness.
units.rightText: Add iniquity unto their iniquity; And let them not come into thy righteousness.

units.leftText: May they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous.
units.rightText: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, And not be written with the righteous.

units.leftText: But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God.
units.rightText: But I am poor and sorrowful: Let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.

units.leftText: I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving.
units.rightText: I will praise the name of God with a song, And will magnify him with thanksgiving.

units.leftText: And this will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
units.rightText: And it will please Jehovah better than an ox, Or a bullock that hath horns and hoofs.

units.leftText: The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts be revived!
units.rightText: The meek have seen it, and are glad: Ye that seek after God, let your heart live.

units.leftText: For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people.
units.rightText: For Jehovah heareth the needy, And despiseth not his prisoners.

units.leftText: Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
units.rightText: Let heaven and earth praise him, The seas, and everything that moveth therein.

units.leftText: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.
units.rightText: For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah; And they shall abide there, and have it in possession.

units.leftText: The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will settle in it.
units.rightText: The seed also of his servants shall inherit it; And they that love his name shall dwell therein.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. Of David. To bring remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me!
units.rightText: Make haste, O God, to deliver me; Make haste to help me, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.
units.rightText: Let them be put to shame and confounded That seek after my soul: Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor That delight in my hurt.

units.leftText: May those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame.
units.rightText: Let them be turned back by reason of their shame That say, Aha, aha.

units.leftText: May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “Let God be magnified!”
units.rightText: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; And let such as love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified.

units.leftText: But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.
units.rightText: But I am poor and needy; Make haste unto me, O God: Thou art my help and my deliverer; O Jehovah, make no tarrying.

units.leftText: In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
units.rightText: In thee, O Jehovah, do I take refuge: Let me never be put to shame.

units.leftText: In Your justice, rescue and deliver me; incline Your ear and save me.
units.rightText: Deliver me in thy righteousness, and rescue me: Bow down thine ear unto me, and save me.

units.leftText: Be my rock of refuge, where I can always go. Give the command to save me, for You are my rock and my fortress.
units.rightText: Be thou to me a rock of habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: Thou hast given commandment to save me; For thou art my rock and my fortress.

units.leftText: Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless.
units.rightText: Rescue me, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked, Out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.

units.leftText: For You are my hope, O Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
units.rightText: For thou art my hope, O Lord Jehovah: Thou art my trust from my youth.

units.leftText: I have leaned on You since birth; You pulled me from my mother’s womb. My praise is always for You.
units.rightText: By thee have I been holden up from the womb; Thou art he that took me out of my mother’s bowels: My praise shall be continually of thee.

units.leftText: I have become a portent to many, but You are my strong refuge.
units.rightText: I am as a wonder unto many; But thou art my strong refuge.

units.leftText: My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your splendor all day long.
units.rightText: My mouth shall be filled with thy praise, And with thy honor all the day.

units.leftText: Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.
units.rightText: Cast me not off in the time of old age; Forsake me not when my strength faileth.

units.leftText: For my enemies speak against me, and those who lie in wait for my life conspire,
units.rightText: For mine enemies speak concerning me; And they that watch for my soul take counsel together,

units.leftText: saying, “God has forsaken him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”
units.rightText: Saying, God hath forsaken him: Pursue and take him; for there is none to deliver.

units.leftText: Be not far from me, O God. Hurry, O my God, to help me.
units.rightText: O God, be not far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.

units.leftText: May the accusers of my soul be ashamed and consumed; may those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.
units.rightText: Let them be put to shame and consumed that are adversaries to my soul; Let them be covered with reproach and dishonor that seek my hurt.

units.leftText: But I will always hope and will praise You more and more.
units.rightText: But I will hope continually, And will praise thee yet more and more.

units.leftText: My mouth will declare Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long, though I cannot know their full measure.
units.rightText: My mouth shall tell of thy righteousness, And of thy salvation all the day; For I know not the numbers thereof.

units.leftText: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim Your righteousness — Yours alone.
units.rightText: I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord Jehovah: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.

units.leftText: O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.
units.rightText: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth; And hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works.

units.leftText: Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come.
units.rightText: Yea, even when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not, Until I have declared thy strength unto the next generation, Thy might to every one that is to come.

units.leftText: Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, O God, You who have done great things. Who, O God, is like You?
units.rightText: Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high; Thou who hast done great things, O God, who is like unto thee?

units.leftText: Though You have shown me many troubles and misfortunes, You will revive me once again. Even from the depths of the earth You will bring me back up.
units.rightText: Thou, who hast showed us many and sore troubles, Wilt quicken us again, And wilt bring us up again from the depths of the earth.

units.leftText: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.
units.rightText: Increase thou my greatness, And turn again and comfort me.

units.leftText: So I will praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praise to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: I will also praise thee with the psaltery, Even thy truth, O my God: Unto thee will I sing praises with the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: When I sing praise to You my lips will shout for joy, along with my soul, which You have redeemed.
units.rightText: My lips shall shout for joy when I sing praises unto thee; And my soul, which thou hast redeemed.

units.leftText: My tongue will indeed proclaim Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are disgraced and confounded.
units.rightText: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long; For they are put to shame, for they are confounded, that seek my hurt.

units.leftText: Of Solomon. Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness.
units.rightText: Give the king thy judgments, O God, And thy righteousness unto the king’s son.

units.leftText: May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice.
units.rightText: He will judge thy people with righteousness, And thy poor with justice.

units.leftText: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness.
units.rightText: The mountains shall bring peace to the people, And the hills, in righteousness.

units.leftText: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.
units.rightText: He will judge the poor of the people, He will save the children of the needy, And will break in pieces the oppressor.

units.leftText: May they fear him as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains, through all generations.
units.rightText: They shall fear thee while the sun endureth, And so long as the moon, throughout all generations.
leftNotes: 72:5 LXX He shall endure

units.leftText: May he be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.
units.rightText: He will come down like rain upon the mown grass, As showers that water the earth.

units.leftText: May the righteous flourish in his days and prosperity abound until the moon is no more.
units.rightText: In his days shall the righteous flourish, And abundance of peace, till the moon be no more.

units.leftText: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, And from the River unto the ends of the earth.
leftNotes: 72:8 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: May the nomads bow before him, and his enemies lick the dust.
units.rightText: They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; And his enemies shall lick the dust.

units.leftText: May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
units.rightText: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall render tribute: The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.

units.leftText: May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him.
units.rightText: Yea, all kings shall fall down before him; All nations shall serve him.

units.leftText: For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.
units.rightText: For he will deliver the needy when he crieth, And the poor, that hath no helper.

units.leftText: He will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed.
units.rightText: He will have pity on the poor and needy, And the souls of the needy he will save.

units.leftText: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight.
units.rightText: He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence; And precious will their blood be in his sight:

units.leftText: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him; may they bless him all day long.
units.rightText: And they shall live; and to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba: And men shall pray for him continually; They shall bless him all the day long.

units.leftText: May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills. May its fruit trees flourish like the forests of Lebanon, the people of its cities like the grass of the field.
units.rightText: There shall be abundance of grain in the earth upon the top of the mountains; The fruit thereof shall shake like Lebanon: And they of the city shall flourish like grass of the earth.

units.leftText: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed.
units.rightText: His name shall endure for ever; His name shall be continued as long as the sun: And men shall be blessed in him; All nations shall call him happy.
leftNotes: 72:17 Or increase

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah God, the God of Israel, Who only doeth wondrous things:

units.leftText: And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen.
units.rightText: And blessed be his glorious name for ever; And let the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen, and Amen.

units.leftText: Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse.
units.rightText: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended. BOOK III

units.leftText: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
units.rightText: Surely God is good to Israel, Even to such as are pure in heart.

units.leftText: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
units.rightText: But as for me, my feet were almost gone; My steps had well nigh slipped.

units.leftText: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
units.rightText: For I was envious at the arrogant, When I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

units.leftText: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.
units.rightText: For there are no pangs in their death; But their strength is firm.

units.leftText: They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.
units.rightText: They are not in trouble as other men; Neither are they plagued like other men.

units.leftText: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
units.rightText: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck; Violence covereth them as a garment.

units.leftText: From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
units.rightText: Their eyes stand out with fatness: They have more than heart could wish.
leftNotes: 73:7 Literally Their eye bulges with fatness; Syriac From their callous heart proceeds iniquity

units.leftText: They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.
units.rightText: They scoff, and in wickedness utter oppression: They speak loftily.

units.leftText: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
units.rightText: They have set their mouth in the heavens, And their tongue walketh through the earth.

units.leftText: So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
units.rightText: Therefore his people return hither: And waters of a full cup are drained by them.
leftNotes: 73:10 Or His people

units.leftText: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”
units.rightText: And they say, How doth God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?

units.leftText: Behold, these are the wicked — always carefree as they increase their wealth.
units.rightText: Behold, these are the wicked; And, being alway at ease, they increase in riches.

units.leftText: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
units.rightText: Surely in vain have I cleansed my heart, And washed my hands in innocency;

units.leftText: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
units.rightText: For all the day long have I been plagued, And chastened every morning.

units.leftText: If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children.
units.rightText: If I had said, I will speak thus; Behold, I had dealt treacherously with the generation of thy children.

units.leftText: When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight
units.rightText: When I thought how I might know this, It was too painful for me;

units.leftText: until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
units.rightText: Until I went into the sanctuary of God, And considered their latter end.

units.leftText: Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
units.rightText: Surely thou settest them in slippery places: Thou castest them down to destruction.

units.leftText: How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!
units.rightText: How are they become a desolation in a moment! They are utterly consumed with terrors.

units.leftText: Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
units.rightText: As a dream when one awaketh, So, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou wilt despise their image.

units.leftText: When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within,
units.rightText: For my soul was grieved, And I was pricked in my heart:

units.leftText: I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
units.rightText: So brutish was I, and ignorant; I was as a beast before thee.

units.leftText: Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
units.rightText: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: Thou hast holden my right hand.

units.leftText: You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.
units.rightText: Thou wilt guide me with thy counsel, And afterward receive me to glory.

units.leftText: Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
units.rightText: Whom have I in heaven but thee? And there is none upon earth that I desire besides thee.

units.leftText: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
units.rightText: My flesh and my heart faileth; But God is the strength of my heart and my portion for ever.
leftNotes: 73:26 Hebrew rock

units.leftText: Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
units.rightText: For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: Thou hast destroyed all them that play the harlot, departing from thee.

units.leftText: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.
units.rightText: But it is good for me to draw near unto God: I have made the Lord Jehovah my refuge, That I may tell of all thy works.

units.leftText: A Maskil of Asaph. Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
units.rightText: O God, why hast thou cast us off for ever? Why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
leftNotes: 74:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance — Mount Zion, where You dwell.
units.rightText: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast gotten of old, Which thou hast redeemed to be the tribe of thine inheritance; And mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.

units.leftText: Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed.
units.rightText: Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual ruins, All the evil that the enemy hath done in the sanctuary.

units.leftText: Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have unfurled their banners as signs,
units.rightText: Thine adversaries have roared in the midst of thine assembly; They have set up their ensigns for signs.

units.leftText: like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees
units.rightText: They seemed as men that lifted up Axes upon a thicket of trees.

units.leftText: and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.
units.rightText: And now all the carved work thereof They break down with hatchet and hammers.

units.leftText: They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.
units.rightText: They have set thy sanctuary on fire; They have profaned the dwelling-place of thy name by casting it to the ground.

units.leftText: They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land.
units.rightText: They said in their heart, Let us make havoc of them altogether: They have burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.

units.leftText: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.
units.rightText: We see not our signs: There is no more any prophet; Neither is there among us any that knoweth how long.

units.leftText: How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever?
units.rightText: How long, O God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?

units.leftText: Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand? Stretch it out to destroy them!
units.rightText: Why drawest thou back thy hand, even thy right hand? Pluck it out of thy bosom and consume them.
leftNotes: 74:11 Literally From the midst of Your bosom destroy them! or From the midst of Your bosom remove it!

units.leftText: Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.
units.rightText: Yet God is my King of old, Working salvation in the midst of the earth.

units.leftText: You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea;
units.rightText: Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: Thou brakest the heads of the sea-monsters in the waters.

units.leftText: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert.
units.rightText: Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces; Thou gavest him to be food to the people inhabiting the wilderness.

units.leftText: You broke open the fountain and the flood; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
units.rightText: Thou didst cleave fountain and flood: Thou driedst up mighty rivers.

units.leftText: The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.
units.rightText: The day is thine, the night also is thine: Thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
leftNotes: 74:16 Literally the light

units.leftText: You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter.
units.rightText: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: Thou hast made summer and winter.

units.leftText: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
units.rightText: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Jehovah, And that a foolish people hath blasphemed thy name.

units.leftText: Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.
units.rightText: Oh deliver not the soul of thy turtle-dove unto the wild beast: Forget not the life of thy poor for ever.

units.leftText: Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.
units.rightText: Have respect unto the covenant; For the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of violence.

units.leftText: Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.
units.rightText: Oh let not the oppressed return ashamed: Let the poor and needy praise thy name.

units.leftText: Rise up, O God; defend Your cause! Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.
units.rightText: Arise, O God, plead thine own cause: Remember how the foolish man reproacheth thee all the day.

units.leftText: Do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.
units.rightText: Forget not the voice of thine adversaries: The tumult of those that rise up against thee ascendeth continually.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster: To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Psalm of Asaph. A song. We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.
units.rightText: We give thanks unto thee, O God; We give thanks, for thy name is near: Men tell of thy wondrous works.

units.leftText: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.
units.rightText: When I shall find the set time, I will judge uprightly.

units.leftText: When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars. Selah
units.rightText: The earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved: I have set up the pillars of it. [Selah*

units.leftText: I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
units.rightText: I said unto the arrogant, Deal not arrogantly; And to the wicked, Lift not up the horn:

units.leftText: Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck.’”
units.rightText: Lift not up your horn on high; Speak not with a stiff neck.

units.leftText: For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert,
units.rightText: For neither from the east, nor from the west, Nor yet from the south, cometh lifting up.

units.leftText: but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.
units.rightText: But God is the judge: He putteth down one, and lifteth up another.

units.leftText: For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours from His cup, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.
units.rightText: For in the hand of Jehovah there is a cup, and the wine foameth; It is full of mixture, and he poureth out of the same: Surely the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall drain them, and drink them.

units.leftText: But I will proclaim Him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: But I will declare for ever, I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
leftNotes: 75:9 Or proclaim it

units.leftText: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.”
units.rightText: All the horns of the wicked also will I cut off; But the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.
units.rightText: In Judah is God known: His name is great in Israel.

units.leftText: His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion.
units.rightText: In Salem also is his tabernacle, And his dwelling-place in Zion.
leftNotes: 76:2 That is, Jerusalem

units.leftText: There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war. Selah
units.rightText: There he brake the arrows of the bow; The shield, and the sword, and the battle. [Selah*

units.leftText: You are resplendent with light, more majestic than mountains filled with game.
units.rightText: Glorious art thou and excellent, From the mountains of prey.

units.leftText: The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep. No men of might could lift a hand.
units.rightText: The stouthearted are made a spoil, They have slept their sleep; And none of the men of might have found their hands.

units.leftText: At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and rider lie stunned.
units.rightText: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, Both chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep.

units.leftText: You alone are to be feared. When You are angry, who can stand before You?
units.rightText: Thou, even thou, art to be feared; And who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry?

units.leftText: From heaven You pronounced judgment, and the earth feared and was still
units.rightText: Thou didst cause sentence to be heard from heaven; The earth feared, and was still,

units.leftText: when God rose up to judge, to save all the lowly of the earth. Selah
units.rightText: When God arose to judgment, To save all the meek of the earth. [Selah*

units.leftText: Even the wrath of man shall praise You; with the survivors of wrath You will clothe Yourself.
units.rightText: Surely the wrath of man shall praise thee: The residue of wrath shalt thou gird upon thee.
leftNotes: 76:10 Or Surely Your wrath against men brings You praise, and the survivors of Your wrath will be restrained.

units.leftText: Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God; let all the neighboring lands bring tribute to Him who is to be feared.
units.rightText: Vow, and pay unto Jehovah your God: Let all that are round about him bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.

units.leftText: He breaks the spirits of princes; He is feared by the kings of the earth.
units.rightText: He will cut off the spirit of princes: He is terrible to the kings of the earth.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.
units.rightText: I will cry unto God with my voice, Even unto God with my voice; and he will give ear unto me.

units.leftText: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.
units.rightText: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: My hand was stretched out in the night, and slacked not; My soul refused to be comforted.

units.leftText: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah
units.rightText: I remember God, and am disquieted: I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. [Selah*

units.leftText: You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.
units.rightText: Thou holdest mine eyes watching: I am so troubled that I cannot speak.

units.leftText: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.
units.rightText: I have considered the days of old, The years of ancient times.

units.leftText: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:
units.rightText: I call to remembrance my song in the night: I commune with mine own heart; And my spirit maketh diligent search.

units.leftText: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?
units.rightText: Will the Lord cast off for ever? And will he be favorable no more?

units.leftText: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?
units.rightText: Is his lovingkindness clean gone for ever? Doth his promise fail for evermore?

units.leftText: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah
units.rightText: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? Hath he in anger shut up his tender mercies? [Selah*

units.leftText: So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
units.rightText: And I said, This is my infirmity; But I will remember the years of the right hand of the Most High.
leftNotes: 77:10 Or “To this I will appeal: to the years of the right hand of the Most High.”

units.leftText: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
units.rightText: I will make mention of the deeds of Jehovah; For I will remember thy wonders of old.

units.leftText: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.
units.rightText: I will meditate also upon all thy work, And muse on thy doings.

units.leftText: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?
units.rightText: Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary: Who is a great god like unto God?

units.leftText: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.
units.rightText: Thou art the God that doest wonders: Thou hast made known thy strength among the peoples.

units.leftText: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
units.rightText: Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people, The sons of Jacob and Joseph. [Selah*

units.leftText: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.
units.rightText: The waters saw thee, O God; The waters saw thee, they were afraid: The depths also trembled.

units.leftText: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
units.rightText: The clouds poured out water; The skies sent out a sound: Thine arrows also went abroad.

units.leftText: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
units.rightText: The voice of thy thunder was in the whirlwind; The lightnings lightened the world: The earth trembled and shook.

units.leftText: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.
units.rightText: Thy way was in the sea, And thy paths in the great waters, And thy footsteps were not known.
leftNotes: 77:19 Or were unknown

units.leftText: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: Thou leddest thy people like a flock, By the hand of Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Give ear, O my people, to my law: Incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
leftNotes: 78:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
units.rightText: I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old,
leftNotes: 78:2 Or from ancient times; see also LXX; cited in Matthew 13:35|MAT 13:35*

units.leftText: that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.
units.rightText: Which we have heard and known, And our fathers have told us.

units.leftText: We will not hide them from their children but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might and the wonders He has performed.
units.rightText: We will not hide them from their children, Telling to the generation to come the praises of Jehovah, And his strength, and his wondrous works that he hath done.

units.leftText: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,
units.rightText: For he established a testimony in Jacob, And appointed a law in Israel, Which he commanded our fathers, That they should make them known to their children;

units.leftText: that the coming generation would know them— even children yet to be born— to arise and tell their own children
units.rightText: That the generation to come might know them, even the children that should be born; Who should arise and tell them to their children,

units.leftText: that they should put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments.
units.rightText: That they might set their hope in God, And not forget the works of God, But keep his commandments,

units.leftText: Then they will not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
units.rightText: And might not be as their fathers, A stubborn and rebellious generation, A generation that set not their heart aright, And whose spirit was not stedfast with God.

units.leftText: The archers of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle.
units.rightText: The children of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, Turned back in the day of battle.

units.leftText: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.
units.rightText: They kept not the covenant of God, And refused to walk in his law;

units.leftText: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.
units.rightText: And they forgat his doings, And his wondrous works that he had showed them.

units.leftText: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
units.rightText: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, In the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.

units.leftText: He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.
units.rightText: He clave the sea, and caused them to pass through; And he made the waters to stand as a heap.

units.leftText: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.
units.rightText: In the day-time also he led them with a cloud, And all the night with a light of fire.

units.leftText: He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the seas.
units.rightText: He clave rocks in the wilderness, And gave them drink abundantly as out of the depths.

units.leftText: He brought streams from the stone and made water flow down like rivers.
units.rightText: He brought streams also out of the rock, And caused waters to run down like rivers.

units.leftText: But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.
units.rightText: Yet went they on still to sin against him, To rebel against the Most High in the desert.

units.leftText: They willfully tested God by demanding the food they craved.
units.rightText: And they tempted God in their heart By asking food according to their desire.

units.leftText: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
units.rightText: Yea, they spake against God; They said, Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?

units.leftText: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”
units.rightText: Behold, he smote the rock, so that waters gushed out, And streams overflowed; Can he give bread also? Will he provide flesh for his people?

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel,
units.rightText: Therefore Jehovah heard, and was wroth; And a fire was kindled against Jacob, And anger also went up against Israel;

units.leftText: because they did not believe God or rely on His salvation.
units.rightText: Because they believed not in God, And trusted not in his salvation.

units.leftText: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.
units.rightText: Yet he commanded the skies above, And opened the doors of heaven;

units.leftText: He rained down manna for them to eat; He gave them grain from heaven.
units.rightText: And he rained down manna upon them to eat, And gave them food from heaven.
leftNotes: 78:24 Cited in John 6:31|JHN 6:31*

units.leftText: Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.
units.rightText: Man did eat the bread of the mighty: He sent them food to the full.

units.leftText: He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.
units.rightText: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens; And by his power he guided the south wind.

units.leftText: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
units.rightText: He rained flesh also upon them as the dust, And winged birds as the sand of the seas:

units.leftText: He felled them in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
units.rightText: And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, Round about their habitations.

units.leftText: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.
units.rightText: So they did eat, and were well filled; And he gave them their own desire.

units.leftText: Yet before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths,
units.rightText: They were not estranged from that which they desired, Their food was yet in their mouths,

units.leftText: God’s anger flared against them, and He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel.
units.rightText: When the anger of God went up against them, And slew of the fattest of them, And smote down the young men of Israel.

units.leftText: In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; despite His wonderful works, they did not believe.
units.rightText: For all this they sinned still, And believed not in his wondrous works.

units.leftText: So He ended their days in futility, and their years in sudden terror.
units.rightText: Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, And their years in terror.
leftNotes: 78:33 Or in vapor

units.leftText: When He slew them, they would seek Him; they repented and searched for God.
units.rightText: When he slew them, then they inquired after him; And they returned and sought God earnestly.

units.leftText: And they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
units.rightText: And they remembered that God was their rock, And the Most High God their redeemer.
leftNotes: 78:35 Hebrew El-Elyon

units.leftText: But they deceived Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues.
units.rightText: But they flattered him with their mouth, And lied unto him with their tongue.

units.leftText: Their hearts were disloyal to Him, and they were unfaithful to His covenant.
units.rightText: For their heart was not right with him, Neither were they faithful in his covenant.

units.leftText: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
units.rightText: But he, being merciful, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: Yea, many a time turned he his anger away, And did not stir up all his wrath.

units.leftText: He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return.
units.rightText: And he remembered that they were but flesh, A wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.

units.leftText: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
units.rightText: How oft did they rebel against him in the wilderness, And grieve him in the desert!

units.leftText: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: And they turned again and tempted God, And provoked the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: They did not remember His power — the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
units.rightText: They remembered not his hand, Nor the day when he redeemed them from the adversary;
leftNotes: 78:42 Or His hand

units.leftText: when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
units.rightText: How he set his signs in Egypt, And his wonders in the field of Zoan,

units.leftText: He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink.
units.rightText: And turned their rivers into blood, And their streams, so that they could not drink.

units.leftText: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.
units.rightText: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; And frogs, which destroyed them.

units.leftText: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.
units.rightText: He gave also their increase unto the caterpillar, And their labor unto the locust.

units.leftText: He killed their vines with hailstones and their sycamore-figs with sleet.
units.rightText: He destroyed their vines with hail, And their sycomore-trees with frost.
leftNotes: 78:47 Or frost or driving rain

units.leftText: He abandoned their cattle to the hail and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
units.rightText: He gave over their cattle also to the hail, And their flocks to hot thunderbolts.

units.leftText: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity— a band of destroying angels.
units.rightText: He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, Wrath, and indignation, and trouble, A band of angels of evil.

units.leftText: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
units.rightText: He made a path for his anger; He spared not their soul from death, But gave their life over to the pestilence,

units.leftText: He struck all the firstborn of Egypt, the virility in the tents of Ham.
units.rightText: And smote all the first-born in Egypt, The chief of their strength in the tents of Ham.

units.leftText: He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
units.rightText: But he led forth his own people like sheep, And guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

units.leftText: He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.
units.rightText: And he led them safely, so that they feared not; But the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

units.leftText: He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired.
units.rightText: And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, To this mountain, which his right hand had gotten.

units.leftText: He drove out nations before them and apportioned their inheritance; He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
units.rightText: He drove out the nations also before them, And allotted them for an inheritance by line, And made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.

units.leftText: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
units.rightText: Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, And kept not his testimonies;

units.leftText: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.
units.rightText: But turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers: They were turned aside like a deceitful bow.

units.leftText: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.
units.rightText: For they provoked him to anger with their high places, And moved him to jealousy with their graven images.

units.leftText: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.
units.rightText: When God heard this, he was wroth, And greatly abhorred Israel;

units.leftText: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
units.rightText: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, The tent which he placed among men;

units.leftText: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.
units.rightText: And delivered his strength into captivity, And his glory into the adversary’s hand.

units.leftText: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.
units.rightText: He gave his people over also unto the sword, And was wroth with his inheritance.

units.leftText: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
units.rightText: Fire devoured their young men; And their virgins had no marriage-song.

units.leftText: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
units.rightText: Their priests fell by the sword; And their widows made no lamentation.

units.leftText: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.
units.rightText: Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, Like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.

units.leftText: He beat back His foes; He put them to everlasting shame.
units.rightText: And he smote his adversaries backward: He put them to a perpetual reproach.

units.leftText: He rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim.
units.rightText: Moreover he refused the tent of Joseph, And chose not the tribe of Ephraim,

units.leftText: But He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.
units.rightText: But chose the tribe of Judah, The mount Zion which he loved.

units.leftText: He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever.
units.rightText: And he built his sanctuary like the heights, Like the earth which he hath established for ever.

units.leftText: He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
units.rightText: He chose David also his servant, And took him from the sheepfolds:

units.leftText: from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance.
units.rightText: From following the ewes that have their young he brought him, To be the shepherd of Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.

units.leftText: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
units.rightText: So he was their shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, And guided them by the skilfulness of his hands.

units.leftText: A Psalm of Asaph. The nations, O God, have invaded Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.
units.rightText: O God, the nations are come into thine inheritance; Thy holy temple have they defiled; They have laid Jerusalem in heaps.

units.leftText: They have given the corpses of Your servants as food to the birds of the air, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth.
units.rightText: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be food unto the birds of the heavens, The flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

units.leftText: They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury the dead.
units.rightText: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; And there was none to bury them.

units.leftText: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around us.
units.rightText: We are become a reproach to our neighbors, A scoffing and derision to them that are round about us.

units.leftText: How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire?
units.rightText: How long, O Jehovah? wilt thou be angry for ever? Shall thy jealousy burn like fire?

units.leftText: Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, on the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name,
units.rightText: Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that know thee not, And upon the kingdoms that call not upon thy name.

units.leftText: for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his homeland.
units.rightText: For they have devoured Jacob, And laid waste his habitation.

units.leftText: Do not hold past sins against us; let Your compassion come quickly, for we are brought low.
units.rightText: Remember not against us the iniquities of our forefathers: Let thy tender mercies speedily meet us; For we are brought very low.

units.leftText: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name.
units.rightText: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name; And deliver us, and forgive our sins, for thy name’s sake.

units.leftText: Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, make known among the nations Your vengeance for the bloodshed of Your servants.
units.rightText: Wherefore should the nations say, Where is their God? Let the avenging of the blood of thy servants which is shed Be known among the nations in our sight.

units.leftText: May the groans of the captives reach You; by the strength of Your arm preserve those condemned to death.
units.rightText: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before thee: According to the greatness of thy power preserve thou those that are appointed to death;

units.leftText: Pay back into the laps of our neighbors sevenfold the reproach they hurled at You, O Lord.
units.rightText: And render unto our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom Their reproach, wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.

units.leftText: Then we Your people, the sheep of Your pasture, will thank You forever; from generation to generation we will declare Your praise.
units.rightText: So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture Will give thee thanks for ever: We will show forth thy praise to all generations.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm of Asaph. Hear us, O Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; You who sit enthroned between the cherubim,
units.rightText: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; Thou that sittest above the cherubim, shine forth.

units.leftText: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.
units.rightText: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up thy might, And come to save us.

units.leftText: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
units.rightText: Turn us again, O God; And cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.

units.leftText: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
units.rightText: O Jehovah God of hosts, How long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy people?

units.leftText: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.
units.rightText: Thou hast fed them with the bread of tears, And given them tears to drink in large measure.

units.leftText: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
units.rightText: Thou makest us a strife unto our neighbors; And our enemies laugh among themselves.

units.leftText: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
units.rightText: Turn us again, O God of hosts; And cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.

units.leftText: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
units.rightText: Thou broughtest a vine out of Egypt: Thou didst drive out the nations, and plantedst it.

units.leftText: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.
units.rightText: Thou preparedst room before it, And it took deep root, and filled the land.

units.leftText: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
units.rightText: The mountains were covered with the shadow of it, And the boughs thereof were like cedars of God.

units.leftText: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
units.rightText: It sent out its branches unto the sea, And its shoots unto the River.
leftNotes: 80:11 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea
80:11 That is, the Euphrates

units.leftText: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
units.rightText: Why hast thou broken down its walls, So that all they that pass by the way do pluck it?

units.leftText: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
units.rightText: The boar out of the wood doth ravage it, And the wild beasts of the field feed on it.

units.leftText: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—
units.rightText: Turn again, we beseech thee, O God of hosts: Look down from heaven, and behold, and visit this vine,

units.leftText: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
units.rightText: And the stock which thy right hand planted, And the branch that thou madest strong for thyself.

units.leftText: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
units.rightText: It is burned with fire, it is cut down: They perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.

units.leftText: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
units.rightText: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, Upon the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself.

units.leftText: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.
units.rightText: So shall we not go back from thee: Quicken thou us, and we will call upon thy name.

units.leftText: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
units.rightText: Turn us again, O Jehovah God of hosts; Cause thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: Sing aloud unto God our strength: Make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
leftNotes: 81:1 Gittith is probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalms 8 and 84.

units.leftText: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.
units.rightText: Raise a song, and bring hither the timbrel, The pleasant harp with the psaltery.

units.leftText: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.
units.rightText: Blow the trumpet at the new moon, At the full moon, on our feast-day.

units.leftText: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: For it is a statute for Israel, An ordinance of the God of Jacob.

units.leftText: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language:
units.rightText: He appointed it in Joseph for a testimony, When he went out over the land of Egypt, Where I heard a language that I knew not.
leftNotes: 81:5 Or in Joseph

units.leftText: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
units.rightText: I removed his shoulder from the burden: His hands were freed from the basket.

units.leftText: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
units.rightText: Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder; I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. [Selah*
leftNotes: 81:7 Meribah means quarreling; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!
units.rightText: Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wouldest hearken unto me!

units.leftText: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.
units.rightText: There shall no strange god be in thee; Neither shalt thou worship any foreign god.

units.leftText: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
units.rightText: I am Jehovah thy God, Who brought thee up out of the land of Egypt: Open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

units.leftText: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.
units.rightText: But my people hearkened not to my voice; And Israel would none of me.

units.leftText: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.
units.rightText: So I let them go after the stubbornness of their heart, That they might walk in their own counsels.

units.leftText: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,
units.rightText: Oh that my people would hearken unto me, That Israel would walk in my ways!

units.leftText: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
units.rightText: I would soon subdue their enemies, And turn my hand against their adversaries.

units.leftText: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.
units.rightText: The haters of Jehovah should submit themselves unto him: But their time should endure for ever.

units.leftText: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
units.rightText: He would feed them also with the finest of the wheat; And with honey out of the rock would I satisfy thee.

units.leftText: A Psalm of Asaph. God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:
units.rightText: God standeth in the congregation of God; He judgeth among the gods.

units.leftText: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
units.rightText: How long will ye judge unjustly, And respect the persons of the wicked? [Selah*
leftNotes: 82:2 Or How long will you defend the unjust

units.leftText: Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.
units.rightText: Judge the poor and fatherless: Do justice to the afflicted and destitute.

units.leftText: Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.
units.rightText: Rescue the poor and needy: Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.

units.leftText: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
units.rightText: They know not, neither do they understand; They walk to and fro in darkness: All the foundations of the earth are shaken.

units.leftText: I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
units.rightText: I said, Ye are gods, And all of you sons of the Most High.
leftNotes: 82:6 Cited in John 10:34|JHN 10:34*

units.leftText: But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”
units.rightText: Nevertheless ye shall die like men, And fall like one of the princes.

units.leftText: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.
units.rightText: Arise, O God, judge the earth; For thou shalt inherit all the nations.

units.leftText: A song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
units.rightText: O God, keep not thou silence: Hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
leftNotes: 83:1 Or deaf

units.leftText: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
units.rightText: For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult; And they that hate thee have lifted up the head.

units.leftText: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,
units.rightText: They take crafty counsel against thy people, And consult together against thy hidden ones.

units.leftText: saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
units.rightText: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; That the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.

units.leftText: For with one mind they plot together; they form an alliance against You—
units.rightText: For they have consulted together with one consent; Against thee do they make a covenant:

units.leftText: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,
units.rightText: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagarenes;

units.leftText: of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
units.rightText: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre:

units.leftText: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah
units.rightText: Assyria also is joined with them; They have helped the children of Lot. [Selah*

units.leftText: Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,
units.rightText: Do thou unto them as unto Midian, As to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the river Kishon;

units.leftText: who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
units.rightText: Who perished at Endor, Who became as dung for the earth.

units.leftText: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
units.rightText: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb; Yea, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna;

units.leftText: who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
units.rightText: Who said, Let us take to ourselves in possession The habitations of God.

units.leftText: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
units.rightText: O my God, make them like the whirling dust; As stubble before the wind.

units.leftText: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
units.rightText: As the fire that burneth the forest, And as the flame that setteth the mountains on fire,

units.leftText: so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
units.rightText: So pursue them with thy tempest, And terrify them with thy storm.

units.leftText: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
units.rightText: Fill their faces with confusion, That they may seek thy name, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.
units.rightText: Let them be put to shame and dismayed for ever; Yea, let them be confounded and perish;

units.leftText: May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
units.rightText: That they may know that thou alone, whose name is Jehovah, Art the Most High over all the earth.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!
units.rightText: How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Jehovah of hosts!
leftNotes: 84:1 Gittith is probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalms 8 and 81.

units.leftText: My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
units.rightText: My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of Jehovah; My heart and my flesh cry out unto the living God.

units.leftText: Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
units.rightText: Yea, the sparrow hath found her a house, And the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, Even thine altars, O Jehovah of hosts, My King, and my God.

units.leftText: How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah
units.rightText: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: They will be still praising thee. [Selah*

units.leftText: Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; In whose heart are the highways to Zion.

units.leftText: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; even the autumn rain covers it with pools.
units.rightText: Passing through the valley of Weeping they make it a place of springs; Yea, the early rain covereth it with blessings.
leftNotes: 84:6 Or Valley of Poplars
84:6 Or with blessings

units.leftText: They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
units.rightText: They go from strength to strength; Every one of them appeareth before God in Zion.

units.leftText: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
units.rightText: O Jehovah God of hosts, hear my prayer; Give ear, O God of Jacob. [Selah*

units.leftText: Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.
units.rightText: Behold, O God our shield, And look upon the face of thine anointed.

units.leftText: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
units.rightText: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, Than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.

units.leftText: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
units.rightText: For Jehovah God is a sun and a shield: Jehovah will give grace and glory; No good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.

units.leftText: O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!
units.rightText: O Jehovah of hosts, Blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.

units.leftText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.
units.rightText: Jehovah, thou hast been favorable unto thy land; Thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
leftNotes: 85:1 Or restored the fortunes of Jacob

units.leftText: You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin. Selah
units.rightText: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people; Thou hast covered all their sin. [Selah*

units.leftText: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.
units.rightText: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath; Thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness of thine anger.

units.leftText: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
units.rightText: Turn us, O God of our salvation, And cause thine indignation toward us to cease.

units.leftText: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?
units.rightText: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? Wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?

units.leftText: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?
units.rightText: Wilt thou not quicken us again, That thy people may rejoice in thee?

units.leftText: Show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
units.rightText: Show us thy lovingkindness, O Jehovah, And grant us thy salvation.

units.leftText: I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.
units.rightText: I will hear what God Jehovah will speak; For he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: But let them not turn again to folly.

units.leftText: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.
units.rightText: Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him, That glory may dwell in our land.

units.leftText: Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.
units.rightText: Mercy and truth are met together; Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.

units.leftText: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
units.rightText: Truth springeth out of the earth; And righteousness hath looked down from heaven.

units.leftText: The LORD will indeed provide what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
units.rightText: Yea, Jehovah will give that which is good; And our land shall yield its increase.

units.leftText: Righteousness will go before Him to prepare the way for His steps.
units.rightText: Righteousness shall go before him, And shall make his footsteps a way to walk in.

units.leftText: A prayer of David. Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
units.rightText: Bow down thine ear, O Jehovah, and answer me; For I am poor and needy.

units.leftText: Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You are my God; save Your servant who trusts in You.
units.rightText: Preserve my soul; for I am godly: O thou my God, save thy servant that trusteth in thee.

units.leftText: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long.
units.rightText: Be merciful unto me, O Lord; For unto thee do I cry all the day long.

units.leftText: Bring joy to Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
units.rightText: Rejoice the soul of thy servant; For unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.

units.leftText: For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.
units.rightText: For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive, And abundant in lovingkindness unto all them that call upon thee.

units.leftText: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and attend to my plea for mercy.
units.rightText: Give ear, O Jehovah, unto my prayer; And hearken unto the voice of my supplications.

units.leftText: In the day of my distress I call on You, because You answer me.
units.rightText: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee; For thou wilt answer me.

units.leftText: O Lord, there is none like You among the gods, nor any works like Yours.
units.rightText: There is none like unto thee among the gods, O Lord; Neither are there any works like unto thy works.

units.leftText: All the nations You have made will come and bow before You, O Lord, and they will glorify Your name.
units.rightText: All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; And they shall glorify thy name.

units.leftText: For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God.
units.rightText: For thou art great, and doest wondrous things: Thou art God alone.

units.leftText: Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name.
units.rightText: Teach me thy way, O Jehovah; I will walk in thy truth: Unite my heart to fear thy name.

units.leftText: I will praise You, O Lord my God, with all my heart; I will glorify Your name forever.
units.rightText: I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart; And I will glorify thy name for evermore.

units.leftText: For great is Your loving devotion to me; You have delivered me from the depths of Sheol.
units.rightText: For great is thy lovingkindness toward me; And thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.

units.leftText: The arrogant rise against me, O God; a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they have no regard for You.
units.rightText: O God, the proud are risen up against me, And a company of violent men have sought after my soul, And have not set thee before them.

units.leftText: But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.
units.rightText: But thou, O Lord, art a God merciful and gracious, Slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth.

units.leftText: Turn to me and have mercy; grant Your strength to Your servant; save the son of Your maidservant.
units.rightText: Oh turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; Give thy strength unto thy servant, And save the son of thy handmaid.

units.leftText: Show me a sign of Your goodness, that my enemies may see and be ashamed; for You, O LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
units.rightText: Show me a token for good, That they who hate me may see it, and be put to shame, Because thou, Jehovah, hast helped me, and comforted me.

units.leftText: A Psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. He has founded His city on the holy mountains.
units.rightText: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
leftNotes: 87:1 Literally His foundation is on the holy mountains

units.leftText: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
units.rightText: Jehovah loveth the gates of Zion More than all the dwellings of Jacob.

units.leftText: Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God. Selah
units.rightText: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. [Selah*

units.leftText: “I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me — along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush — when I say, ‘This one was born in Zion.’”
units.rightText: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon as among them that know me: Behold, Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia: This one was born there.
leftNotes: 87:4 Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt.
87:4 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: And it will be said of Zion: “This one and that one were born in her, and the Most High Himself will establish her.”
units.rightText: Yea, of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one was born in her; And the Most High himself will establish her.

units.leftText: The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: “This one was born in Zion.” Selah
units.rightText: Jehovah will count, when he writeth up the peoples, This one was born there. [Selah*

units.leftText: Singers and pipers will proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.”
units.rightText: They that sing as well as they that dance shall say, All my fountains are in thee.

units.leftText: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee.
leftNotes: 88:1 Mahalath Leannothis probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 53:1|PSA 53:1*.
88:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: May my prayer come before You; incline Your ear to my cry.
units.rightText: Let my prayer enter into thy presence; Incline thine ear unto my cry.

units.leftText: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
units.rightText: For my soul is full of troubles, And my life draweth nigh unto Sheol.

units.leftText: I am counted among those descending to the Pit. I am like a man without strength.
units.rightText: I am reckoned with them that go down into the pit; I am as a man that hath no help,

units.leftText: I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care.
units.rightText: Cast off among the dead, Like the slain that lie in the grave, Whom thou rememberest no more, And they are cut off from thy hand.

units.leftText: You have laid me in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths.
units.rightText: Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, In dark places, in the deeps.

units.leftText: Your wrath weighs heavily upon me; all Your waves have submerged me. Selah
units.rightText: Thy wrath lieth hard upon me, And thou hast afflicted me with all thy waves. [Selah*

units.leftText: You have removed my friends from me; You have made me repulsive to them; I am confined and cannot escape.
units.rightText: Thou hast put mine acquaintance far from me; Thou hast made me an abomination unto them: I am shut up, and I cannot come forth.

units.leftText: My eyes grow dim with grief. I call to You daily, O LORD; I spread out my hands to You.
units.rightText: Mine eye wasteth away by reason of affliction: I have called daily upon thee, O Jehovah; I have spread forth my hands unto thee.

units.leftText: Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You? Selah
units.rightText: Wilt thou show wonders to the dead? Shall they that are deceased arise and praise thee? [Selah*

units.leftText: Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon ?
units.rightText: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? Or thy faithfulness in Destruction?
leftNotes: 88:11 Abaddon means Destruction.

units.leftText: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
units.rightText: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? And thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

units.leftText: But to You, O LORD, I cry for help; in the morning my prayer comes before You.
units.rightText: But unto thee, O Jehovah, have I cried; And in the morning shall my prayer come before thee.

units.leftText: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?
units.rightText: Jehovah, why castest thou off my soul? Why hidest thou thy face from me?

units.leftText: From my youth I was afflicted and near death. I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.
units.rightText: I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up: While I suffer thy terrors I am distracted.

units.leftText: Your wrath has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
units.rightText: Thy fierce wrath is gone over me; Thy terrors have cut me off.

units.leftText: All day long they engulf me like water; they enclose me on every side.
units.rightText: They came round about me like water all the day long; They compassed me about together.

units.leftText: You have removed my beloved and my friend; darkness is my closest companion.
